clue.text: Kind of desecration, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of desecration might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A question about what sort of sacrilege something counts as.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'type of', but 'Kind' is an adjective and the definition; 'of' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind person is thoughtful and attentive towards others, the very sense of the answer.

clue.text: Harmony line

definitions.meaning: harmony as a state of peaceful arrangement and calm
a line as a sequence or arrangement, things set out one after another

explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful arrangement is one sense of the word, and a sequence such as 'in alphabetical' arrangement is the other.

clue.text: Attendant in a mess (that is official of course)

definitions.meaning: a servant who looks after diners in a ship's or college's dining hall
an official who oversees a racecourse meeting

explanation.walkthrough: '(that is' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the waiter-attendant in a ship's mess and a race-meeting official.

clue.text: Australian port for the naturalist

definitions.meaning: the capital of Australia's Northern Territory, a harbour city
Charles, author of On the Origin of Species

explanation.definitionFit: The Northern Territory harbour city and the evolution theorist share one surname.

clue.text: This warbler gives us a bloody shock

parts.note: bloody describes the colour of blood, red
a start is a sudden shock or jolt

explanation.surface: A bird whose name promises a gory fright.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a small songbird of the chat family, once grouped with the warblers, with a russet tail.

clue.text: The Queen of Hearts' smaller product?

definitions.text: The Queen of Hearts' smaller product?

parts.words: The Queen of Hearts' smaller product?
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme Queen of Hearts baked tarts, so a little one of her bakes is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: A small pastry case with filling is a diminutive of the baked goods the rhyme's queen made.

clue.text: Wrecked yacht panned as offensively second-rate

indicators.note: a wrecked thing is broken up, so the letters of these words are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A ruined boat gets slated by the critics as shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods both of low quality and unpleasant are described by this idiom.

clue.text: Attests at tests?

definitions.meaning: what a cricket captain does to close an innings in Test matches

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain may end his side's batting innings early by announcing it closed; Test matches are international cricket games.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal statement is one sense; closing an innings in cricket is the other.

clue.text: Poetry shy chap turns out as treatment from 23

indicators.note: turns out signals the letters of these words being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A timid fellow's verse emerges as therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is the answer to 23-across, the famous psychiatrist; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking cure is the kind of mental treatment practised by the famous Viennese shrink.

clue.text: Hospital border may be one

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an edge is a border or margin

explanation.surface: A remark about the boundary around a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be one' refers back to 'border': the answer may be a border, as a row of bushes round a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of shrubs often forms the boundary of a field or garden, so it can be a border.

clue.text: Like Plain Will without a jockey

definitions.meaning: a will with no added clauses or codicils attached
a horse running loose after unseating whoever was on its back

explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added clause to a document, and also a jockey; lacking either earns the word.

clue.text: Intent, would you say, this daring young man?

definitions.text: Intent, would you say, this daring young man?

parts.words: Intent, would you say, this daring young man?
parts.note: read 'Intent' as 'in tent': the daring young man on the flying trapeze performs under the circus big top

explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze artist performs high in the air, typically inside a circus big top.

clue.text: Schubert's music was in this time, just for show

definitions.text: Schubert's music was in this time, just for show

parts.words: Schubert's music was in this time, just for show
parts.note: an operetta built from Schubert's tunes is called '___ Time', a show, so the word is the flower in that title

explanation.definitionFit: The operetta 'Lilac Time' set Schubert's melodies, naming a fragrant purple-flowered shrub.

clue.text: Dish Pa cooked is full of green pests

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of these words are worked over and prepared afresh

explanation.surface: Father's dinner turns out to be crawling with greenfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is full of' is only a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and similar sap-sucking insects are the garden pests named.

clue.text: Banner to make one frown

definitions.meaning: a banner is a large newspaper title across the page
a frown makes a crease across the forehead, a line on the head

explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a big newspaper title; frowning puts a crease across the brow.

clue.text: The creation, we hear, of speech-maker at number ten?

parts.note: an orator is one who makes speeches
IO looks like the figures 10

explanation.surface: Something the Prime Minister's speechwriter might produce at Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Haydn's 'The Creation' is a choral work, one we hear performed; 'number ten' recalls 10 Downing Street, the British PM's residence, but gives the look-alike letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's The Creation is a large sacred work for choir, soloists and orchestra.

clue.text: Becoming panicky when learning to fly

definitions.meaning: a fledgling beats its wings while trying to get airborne

explanation.definitionFit: Getting flustered is one sense; beating wings, as a young bird does, is the other.

clue.text: Assist return and thieved from swelling chambers!.

indicators.note: return means the word for assist comes back, read the other way

parts.note: to aid is to assist
stole means thieved

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to help and rob the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns AID into DIA; 'and' and 'from' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The heartbeat phase when the ventricles relax and fill with blood is this medical term.

clue.text: Dangerous fish released from tube

definitions.meaning: the electric ray, which can give a powerful shock
a naval weapon fired from a submarine's launching tube

explanation.definitionFit: The electric ray shares its name with the self-propelled naval missile launched from a tube.

clue.text: Sudden uprising places church-leaders last

indicators.note: last tells us the church letters go at the end

parts.note: puts means places
the leading letters of church are C and H

explanation.surface: Rebels putting the bishops at the back of the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'etat is a sudden violent seizure of power, as the German loanword describes.

clue.text: People lifting their heads a lot? In bad golf you find it

definitions.text: People lifting their heads a lot?

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of these words are messed up and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A golfer's poor game has them looking skyward a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'find it' are links. The definition is whimsical: the study of flying saucers involves a lot of looking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying unidentified flying objects means a lot of gazing up at the sky.

clue.text: His Wigan pier an alternative to spa?

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a well is a spring or spa

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a northern seaside pier could replace a spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Road to Wigan Pier' is a 1937 book; Wigan is an inland Lancashire town, so its pier is a joke; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Road to Wigan Pier, written about poverty in northern England.

clue.text: The famous shrink from cradle rocking

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of the words cradle rocking

explanation.surface: A celebrated psychiatrist's ideas about infancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, the Austrian psychiatrist who founded individual psychology, is the famous name.

clue.text: Artiste to appear before the queen

indicators.note: before places the stage word ahead of the royal letters

parts.note: to perform is to appear on stage
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: Someone's chance at a Royal Variety show.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer such as a singer or actor is an artiste.

clue.text: Half our capital goes on Middle Eastern fruit

indicators.note: goes on places the city half after the eastern letters

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for Middle Eastern

indicators.note: Half takes just the first three of the city's six letters

parts.note: for a British paper, our capital is London

explanation.surface: Half of London's money is spent on Arab produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A large juicy gourd-family fruit, such as a cantaloupe.

clue.text: North African in a loose jacket

definitions.meaning: a native of Tangier in Morocco
a citrus fruit with easily peeled skin

explanation.definitionFit: A Tangier native shares the name with the loose-skinned mandarin-like citrus.

clue.text: Lower edge of a woodland hybrid

parts.note: a lower is something that lows, as cattle do: an ox
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: Describing the bottom edge of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as 'bottom', but here it means one that lows (moos); 'of a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A primula that is a natural cross of primrose and cowslip, found in woods.

clue.text: Descriptive of The Mousetrap and other records

definitions.text: Descriptive of The Mousetrap and other records

parts.words: Descriptive of The Mousetrap and other records
parts.note: The Mousetrap, the record-breaking London stage show, has run for decades; vinyl albums are also called this

explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is an Agatha Christie play running in London since 1952, the world's longest-running play.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that runs and runs is staged for a long time, and an LP record plays for a long time.
